posts.body_html: Boom! What a beaut! Do you think the blush is anthocyanin or another pigment? I've noticed regular leucs produce it too - the immature and newly opened trap has a bronzy cast below the white that fades to green pretty quickly. Seems like it just stands out more on plants like HCW that "aren't supposed" to have much pigment.

posts.body_html: Well in normal red veined leucos the red veining remains or intensifies over time, while the copper blush below the white on the tube disappears soon after the trap hardens off. Almost like a fading cuprea, but faster. Who knows??

posts.body_html:
Have "Green and white"s from a couple of different sources. They start with pink or tan flushes/veins and all fade to green and white like HCW. Also got some Jerry's seed - end of 2012 and sowed them February last year. One cross, leuco 07-1 x leuco AJ01, has some nice little 8 inch pitchers. Most come out pink veined and intensify to a nice red, one very much so with a red lip. However, two show the green and white trait and fade. Of course, not knowing what Jerry's leuco 07-1 is I can't say I was surprised, but I am very pleased at the color diversity. Can't wait till they get bigger. Also, Jerry's (leuco x purp 101)x leuco HCW #O has produced a plant with short stocky leuco pitchers that fade but so far don't all disappear, just a very few thin red thread veins on the tube.
I have observed my two clones of flava maxima develop the same way. Young pitchers are very flushed red and fade as they grow, losing the last of the color right after they have opened to be an even all-over green.

posts.body_html:
Not yet in full force, but I think this fall show will be on par or possibly better than last year. There's soooo many plants that are spitting out new fall traps, but they won't be open for another 2 weeks or so. In fact, this year looks like it may be the best leuco year here in Northern California, I've never seen so many plants starting to develop fall pitchers like they are now. While these aren't totally impressive, they're worth seeing, Photos taken 8/20/16:












Fingers crossed we'll get some super-white traps this year, to be continued....
